definition: Something that seems bad at first but produces a good result.
example: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise because it pushed her to start a successful business.

definition: Something that has both advantages and harmful consequences.
example: Remote work can be a double-edged sword: it offers freedom but can increase isolation.

definition: Very different from something else, usually in a disappointing way.
example: The final product was a far cry from the ambitious prototype we were shown.

definition: A situation in which the rules or facts are unclear.
example: The law remains a grey area when it comes to ownership of AI-generated work.

definition: An unpleasant thing that must be accepted to achieve a result.
example: Most employees regard the weekly paperwork as a necessary evil.

definition: A course of action likely to lead to increasingly serious problems.
example: Allowing one exception could put the committee on a slippery slope.

definition: To make an already difficult situation worse.
example: His sarcastic reply only added fuel to the fire during the negotiations.

phrase: at the drop of a hat
definition: Immediately and without needing any preparation.
example: She is prepared to travel abroad at the drop of a hat.

definition: Back to the beginning after an attempt has failed.
example: When the funding was withdrawn, the research team was back to square one.

definition: To make an exceptional effort to help or please someone.
example: The support team bent over backwards to resolve the issue before launch.

phrase: bite off more than you can chew
definition: To accept more responsibility than you can manage.
example: By leading three projects at once, he bit off more than he could chew.

definition: To make people feel more relaxed in a new social situation.
example: The facilitator used a short game to break the ice before the workshop.

definition: To work or study until very late at night.
example: We burned the midnight oil to finish the proposal before the deadline.

phrase: by the skin of your teeth
definition: Only just; by the narrowest possible margin.
example: The company avoided bankruptcy by the skin of its teeth.

definition: To stop working on something for the rest of the day.
example: We have solved the main problem, so let's call it a day.

definition: To save time or money by doing something less thoroughly.
example: The contractor cut corners, and the defects became obvious within months.

definition: To set a limit on what you are willing to do or accept.
example: I am willing to negotiate, but I draw the line at compromising safety.

definition: To become too nervous to do something that was planned.
example: She got cold feet shortly before signing the partnership agreement.

definition: To start an activity or process.
example: A preliminary meeting will get the ball rolling on the new strategy.

definition: To conflict with what is normal or with someone's principles.
example: His decision to share the data openly went against the grain in that industry.

phrase: hit the nail on the head
definition: To describe the exact cause or truth of a situation.
example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the problem was poor communication.

definition: Over a long period of time rather than immediately.
example: Investing in staff training will save money in the long run.

definition: To prevent a problem or threat from approaching or worsening.
example: Regular maintenance helped keep major technical failures at bay.

definition: To make every possible effort to find or achieve something.
example: Investigators promised to leave no stone unturned in their search for evidence.

definition: To be too late to take advantage of an opportunity.
example: Companies that ignore renewable energy may miss the boat entirely.

definition: To understand someone well because you think in a similar way.
example: The designers were on the same wavelength from the start of the project.

definition: To argue against an idea in order to test it, even if you agree with it.
example: Let me play devil's advocate and question whether demand will remain stable.

definition: To use personal influence to make something happen.
example: He denied pulling strings to secure the appointment.

phrase: put all your eggs in one basket
definition: To depend entirely on one plan or resource.
example: Relying on a single client means putting all your eggs in one basket.

definition: To understand a meaning that is implied rather than stated.
example: Reading between the lines, the report suggests that further cuts are likely.

definition: A practical guideline based on experience rather than exact science.
example: As a rule of thumb, keep an emergency fund covering three months of expenses.

definition: To agree fully with someone.
example: The two departments do not always see eye to eye on spending priorities.

definition: To avoid choosing between two sides of an argument.
example: Policy makers can no longer sit on the fence about data privacy.

phrase: take something with a pinch of salt
definition: To avoid believing something completely.
example: You should take anonymous online reviews with a pinch of salt.

definition: A small visible part of a much larger problem.
example: The reported cases may be only the tip of the iceberg.

definition: To stop trying because success seems impossible.
example: Despite several setbacks, the team refused to throw in the towel.

definition: Feeling slightly ill or lacking energy.
example: I have been feeling under the weather since returning from the conference.

definition: Not yet decided or resolved.
example: The location of the new office is still up in the air.

definition: To survive a difficult period without serious damage.
example: The firm reduced costs and managed to weather the storm.

definition: An event that makes people recognize an urgent problem.
example: The security breach was a wake-up call for the entire organization.

phrase: cross that bridge when we come to it
definition: To deal with a problem only when it actually arises.
example: We may need a larger office, but we will cross that bridge when we come to it.

phrase: have a lot on your plate
definition: To have many tasks or responsibilities at the same time.
example: I cannot take on another assignment because I already have a lot on my plate.

definition: To join a popular activity or trend after it becomes successful.
example: Several competitors jumped on the bandwagon once the service became profitable.

phrase: keep your cards close to your chest
definition: To keep your plans or intentions secret.
example: During the talks, both sides kept their cards close to their chest.

definition: To have just enough money to pay for basic needs.
example: Many families took additional work simply to make ends meet.

definition: To change the rules or requirements unfairly during a process.
example: The client kept moving the goalposts after each revision.

phrase: put your foot in your mouth
definition: To say something embarrassing or offensive by mistake.
example: I put my foot in my mouth by asking about a project that had been cancelled.

definition: To take attention or praise that should belong to someone else.
example: The early announcement stole the researcher's thunder.

phrase: take the bull by the horns
definition: To deal with a difficult situation directly and confidently.
example: She took the bull by the horns and confronted the budget problem immediately.

definition: An obvious major problem that people avoid discussing.
example: The declining sales figures were the elephant in the room at the meeting.

definition: To explain the reason for something or form a particular proportion.
example: Online purchases account for nearly half of the company's revenue.

definition: To support a claim with evidence or make a copy of data.
example: Every conclusion in the report must be backed up by reliable evidence.

definition: To have one main or essential cause or meaning.
example: The disagreement boils down to how the available funds should be allocated.

definition: To stop functioning or divide something into smaller parts for analysis.
example: The figures are broken down by age, region, and income.

definition: To cause a significant change or event to happen.
example: The reforms brought about a gradual improvement in working conditions.

definition: To improve knowledge or a skill that has become less familiar.
example: I need to brush up on my French before the negotiations in Paris.

definition: To cancel an event or planned activity.
example: The organizers called off the outdoor event because of the storm.

definition: To perform or complete a task, study, or instruction.
example: An independent team will carry out a full investigation.

definition: To do something that you did not have time to do earlier.
example: I used the quiet afternoon to catch up on unanswered emails.

definition: To find or meet something unexpectedly.
example: While reviewing the archive, she came across an unpublished letter.

definition: To face a difficult problem, opponent, or restriction.
example: The proposal came up against strong resistance from local residents.

definition: To think of an idea, answer, or plan.
example: The engineers came up with a less expensive solution.

definition: To take strong official action against unwanted or illegal activity.
example: Authorities have promised to crack down on misleading advertisements.

definition: To reduce the amount or frequency of something.
example: The organization is cutting back on travel to reduce emissions.

definition: To abolish or stop using something.
example: The new system does away with the need for paper forms.

definition: To prepare a formal document, plan, or list.
example: The lawyers drew up a revised contract for both parties.

definition: To keep thinking or talking about something, especially something negative.
example: There is little value in dwelling on mistakes that cannot be changed.

definition: To use something as an alternative when other options fail.
example: If negotiations collapse, the company can fall back on its existing agreement.

definition: To understand or find the answer to a problem.
example: Researchers are trying to figure out why the treatment works for some patients.

definition: To do what you promised or complete a planned action.
example: The board must follow through on its commitment to transparency.

definition: To communicate an idea successfully.
example: The documentary gets across the scale of the crisis without exaggeration.

definition: To finally do something after delaying it.
example: I finally got around to reading the full consultation paper.

definition: To avoid punishment after doing something wrong.
example: Companies should not be allowed to get away with hiding essential fees.

definition: To manage with limited money, knowledge, or resources.
example: Small businesses struggled to get by during the downturn.

definition: To support a statement or prediction with evidence.
example: The latest survey bears out our earlier prediction about changing demand.

definition: To examine or review something carefully.
example: Let us go over the evidence once more before reaching a conclusion.

definition: To resolve small problems or disagreements.
example: The teams met to iron out the final technical issues.

definition: To remain at the same level or speed as someone or something.
example: Regulators are struggling to keep up with technological change.

definition: To end workers' employment because there is not enough work or money.
example: The manufacturer may have to lay off several hundred employees.

definition: To be as good as expected or promised.
example: The sequel failed to live up to the standards set by the original film.

definition: To consider someone or something inferior.
example: No profession should be looked down on simply because it involves manual work.

definition: To investigate or examine a problem.
example: A parliamentary committee will look into the allegations.

definition: To compensate for something unpleasant or missing.
example: The excellent location makes up for the apartment's limited space.

definition: To reduce a list of possibilities to a smaller number.
example: We narrowed the candidates down to a shortlist of four.

definition: To stop using something gradually.
example: The country plans to phase out coal-fired power stations.

definition: To state or draw attention to a fact.
example: Several reviewers pointed out a flaw in the methodology.

definition: To formally propose an idea, plan, or candidate.
example: The committee put forward three alternatives for public consultation.

definition: To delay an activity or make someone dislike something.
example: The decision was put off until more evidence became available.

definition: To decide that something is impossible or unsuitable.
example: Doctors have not yet ruled out an underlying infection.

definition: To encounter a person or problem unexpectedly.
example: The construction project ran into legal difficulties.

definition: To explain a plan clearly or begin a journey or task.
example: The report sets out a practical framework for reform.

definition: To continue supporting someone or remain ready to act.
example: The organization stood by its earlier commitment.

definition: To be caused by or originate from something.
example: Many of the delays stem from a shortage of trained staff.

definition: To accept responsibility, work, or a particular role.
example: She took on the task of rebuilding the department.

definition: To reject an offer or reduce volume, heat, or power.
example: He turned down the promotion because it required constant travel.

definition: To develop in a particular way or be discovered to be true.
example: The initial estimates turned out to be far too optimistic.

definition: To consider the advantages and disadvantages before deciding.
example: Investors are weighing up the risks of entering the market.

definition: To find a solution or develop successfully.
example: We need to work out how the costs will be shared.

definition: To direct all attention toward a specific target or issue.
example: The investigation zeroed in on irregular payments.

definition: To succeed in doing something difficult or unexpected.
example: The team pulled off a remarkable recovery in the final quarter.

definition: Used to introduce a commonly held belief without naming specific people.
example: It is widely believed that early intervention produces better long-term outcomes.

definition: Used to introduce an issue that is causing increasing public or expert anxiety.
example: There is growing concern that the policy may deepen regional inequality.

phrase: This raises the question of whether...
translation_tr: Bu, ... olup olmadığı sorusunu gündeme getirir
definition: Used to introduce a logical question created by the previous point.
example: This raises the question of whether the current model is financially sustainable.

definition: Used to state a considered personal viewpoint.
example: From my perspective, the benefits outweigh the short-term costs.

definition: Used to show partial agreement or limited truth.
example: To a certain extent, the criticism is justified.

definition: Used to draw attention to an important supporting detail.
example: It is worth noting that the survey excluded part-time workers.

definition: Used to challenge a belief that many people accept.
example: Contrary to popular belief, the process does not require specialist equipment.

definition: Used to show that a decision or opinion is based on new information.
example: In light of the latest evidence, the guidelines have been revised.

definition: Used to introduce the specific subject being discussed.
example: With regard to funding, no final decision has been made.

definition: Used to focus on one particular aspect of a subject.
example: In terms of reliability, the newer system performs significantly better.

phrase: On the one hand..., on the other hand...
definition: Used to contrast two different sides of an issue.
example: On the one hand, the plan saves money; on the other hand, it reduces flexibility.

definition: Used to emphasize that two related statements are both true.
example: The reform not only reduced costs but also improved access.

definition: Used to show that two things change together.
example: The more transparent the process is, the more likely people are to trust it.

definition: An inverted conditional used to describe a different past result.
example: Had it not been for her intervention, the agreement would have collapsed.

definition: A formal conditional used to identify the factor preventing another result.
example: Were it not for the high cost, the technology would be adopted more widely.

definition: Used to emphasize that a fact is impossible to dispute.
example: There is no denying that public expectations have changed.

definition: Used to introduce something considered obvious.
example: It goes without saying that confidential data must be protected.

definition: Used to identify the most important consideration.
example: What matters most is whether the solution works in practice.

definition: Used to discuss the degree to which something is true or effective.
example: The study examines the extent to which income affects educational outcomes.

definition: Used to identify a likely cause of a result.
example: The improvement can be attributed to better staff training.

definition: Used to introduce the main cause of something.
example: The decline is largely due to changing consumer habits.

definition: Used to offer a cautious explanation rather than a certain conclusion.
example: One possible explanation is that participants misunderstood the instructions.

definition: Used to identify an important difference between two things.
example: A key distinction lies in how the two models treat uncertainty.

phrase: It remains to be seen whether...
definition: Used when the future result is still uncertain.
example: It remains to be seen whether the measures will have a lasting effect.

definition: Used to express strong confidence in a claim.
example: There is little doubt that automation will reshape the industry.

definition: Used to strongly reject an idea, often with inverted word order.
example: By no means should these findings be treated as conclusive.

definition: Used to state a strong prohibition, often followed by inversion.
example: Under no circumstances should personal records be shared without consent.

definition: An inverted structure emphasizing that something happened later.
example: Only after the audit did the scale of the problem become clear.

definition: An inverted structure showing that someone was unaware of what would happen.
example: Little did they know that the decision would transform the entire sector.

definition: Used to show that one past event happened immediately after another.
example: No sooner had the announcement been made than objections began to appear.

definition: Used to show that a second event followed almost immediately.
example: Hardly had the meeting started when the fire alarm went off.

definition: Used to introduce a strong concession before a contrasting statement.
example: Much as I appreciate the effort, the proposal still needs substantial revision.

phrase: While it may be true that...
definition: Used to acknowledge a point before presenting a limitation or contrast.
example: While it may be true that demand is rising, supply remains unpredictable.

definition: Used to qualify or contrast what was just stated.
example: The approach is expensive. That said, it has produced consistently strong results.

definition: A formal way to accept a point before returning to a different argument.
example: Be that as it may, the organization still has a duty to investigate.

definition: Used when an action is taken to protect or benefit something.
example: For the sake of clarity, the two issues should be discussed separately.

definition: Used when one benefit causes harm or loss to something else.
example: Economic growth should not come at the expense of public health.

definition: Used to describe what happens when something is unavailable.
example: In the absence of reliable data, the estimates remain highly uncertain.

definition: Used to identify the event or request that caused an action.
example: In response to public criticism, the agency published the full report.

definition: Used to show that something follows a principle, tradition, or style.
example: In keeping with company policy, all applications were reviewed anonymously.

definition: Used when the result does not depend on a condition.
example: The rule applies regardless of whether the transaction was completed online.

definition: Used to state a condition that must be satisfied.
example: Employees may work remotely provided that their manager approves the arrangement.

definition: Used to state the condition under which something is acceptable.
example: The method is reliable as long as the samples are stored correctly.

definition: A formal phrase limiting a statement to a particular degree or aspect.
example: The policy is effective insofar as it addresses immediate risks.

phrase: To the best of my knowledge,...
definition: Used to make a claim while acknowledging that your information may be incomplete.
example: To the best of my knowledge, no formal complaint has been submitted.

definition: Used to focus a statement on one person, subject, or aspect.
example: As far as data security is concerned, the proposal lacks sufficient detail.

phrase: There is a tendency for... to...
definition: Used to describe a recurring or general pattern.
example: There is a tendency for temporary measures to become permanent.

phrase: It would be misleading to claim that...
definition: Used to reject an oversimplified or inaccurate conclusion.
example: It would be misleading to claim that one factor caused the entire decline.

phrase: This should not be confused with...
definition: Used to distinguish a concept from a similar but different one.
example: Efficiency should not be confused with simply working faster.

definition: Used to introduce a contrast or qualification after making a point.
example: The evidence is limited. Having said that, the initial results are encouraging.
